caption: What if you squeezed a pencil into a diamond? First surprise: pencil 'lead' has no lead in it. It's graphite mixed with clay, and graphite is carbon, the same element a diamond is made of. The difference is how the atoms are arranged: soft sliding sheets in graphite, a locked super-strong grid in diamond. To squeeze one into the other you'd need roughly 50,000 times normal air pressure and well over 1,000 °C. Nature does it around 200 km underground, then rare volcanic eruptions carry diamonds up. Until 1725, every diamond on Earth came from India, from the river gravels around Golconda. Today about 90% of the world's diamonds are cut and polished in Surat. In 1954, a lab first made diamond using about 100,000 atmospheres of pressure. Plot twist: diamonds can burn! Heat one in very hot air and it turns into carbon dioxide gas. Would YOU rather have a pencil or a diamond? 👇
